title: Integral derived tensor: lower bound and torsion cohomology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use the small etale derived category $D(T_{\Et})=D(\Ab(T_{\Et}))$ and its cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $A,B\in D(T_{\Et})$ and $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy $\mathcal H^i(A)=0$ for $i<a$ and $\mathcal H^j(B)=0$ for $j<b$. For the ordinary derived tensor product over $\mathbf Z$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], one has
$$
\mathcal H^r(A\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}B)=0\qquad(r<a+b-1).
$$
If, in addition, every $\mathcal H^i(A)$ is a torsion abelian sheaf (as defined in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]), then every $\mathcal H^r(A\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}B)$ is a torsion abelian sheaf. No common integer annihilating these sheaves, no constructibility assumption, and no condition on the residue characteristics of $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0F0F, lemma-projection-formula-proper, proof: the two paragraphs beginning "Since Z has global dimension 1" and "Moreover"; lower-bound inequalities corrected as explained in report.md.

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $x:s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. By [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules], applied to $K=K^{\rm sep}=\Omega$, stalk at the identity geometric point gives an additive equivalence $S:\mathrm{Ab}(s_{\Et})\simeq\mathrm{Ab}$: the Galois group is trivial. This equivalence is exact, since an equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels. It carries sheaf tensor to ordinary integer tensor: under its compatible equivalence on sheaves of sets and group laws, bilinear morphisms correspond to bilinear maps of groups, and hence the representing tensor objects correspond. As an equivalence it preserves direct sums. Thus its termwise extension preserves cohomology, total tensor complexes and K-flatness in both directions: test acyclicity after tensoring with an arbitrary complex, and use the inverse equivalence to range over all such complexes. The K-flat construction in [def-kun-derived-tensor] consequently identifies its derived tensor with the ordinary derived tensor of abelian groups. Now [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] and [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], applied to $x$ and integer coefficients, identify the derived stalk of $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}B$ with $A_x\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}B_x$ in $D(\mathbf Z)$. Exactness [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives
$$H^i(A_x)=\mathcal H^i(A)_x,\quad H^j(B_x)=\mathcal H^j(B)_x,\quad H^r(A_x\otimes^{\mathbf L}B_x)=\mathcal H^r(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B)_x.$$
In particular the two stalk complexes retain the bounds $a,b$. This stalk comparison imposes no characteristic restriction.

proof.text: Choose cochain representatives $C,D$ of $A_x,B_x$. Replace them by $\tau_{\ge a}C,\tau_{\ge b}D$, respectively. By the explicit good-truncation formulas in [def-kun-truncations], the maps from the original representatives to these are quasi-isomorphisms, because the removed cohomology is zero; hence we may take $C^i=0$ for $i<a$ and $D^j=0$ for $j<b$. For $m,n\in\mathbf N$ put $C_m=\tau_{\le a+m}C$ and $D_n=\tau_{\le b+n}D$. These are bounded complexes, retain the same lower cohomological bounds, and have transition maps to the next truncation. Their termwise colimits are $C,D$: in each fixed degree the system eventually consists of the original term and identity maps. No bounded-below flat or free replacement of the sheaf complexes is asserted.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-integral-bounded-kunneth-exact] to the bounded derived abelian groups $C_m,D_n$. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$ this gives
$$0\to\bigoplus_{i+j=r}H^i(C_m)\otimes H^j(D_n)\to H^r(C_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathbf Z}D_n)\to\bigoplus_{i+j=r+1}\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z}_1(H^i(C_m),H^j(D_n))\to0.$$
The nonzero summands can only have $i\ge a,j\ge b$. Therefore if $r<a+b-1$ both outer groups are zero: $r<a+b$ and $r+1<a+b$. Exactness forces $H^r(C_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}D_n)=0$. The lemma is only being applied to bounded objects, exactly as in its statement.

Use [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-derived-tensor] with $R=A=\mathbf Z$ on the two sequential diagrams of step 2; $\mathbf N$ with its usual order is a small filtered category. We need a symmetry natural in both ordinary derived factors. The equivalence $S$ of step 1 supplies it from the unit's own [lem-kun-tensor-sym], applied on $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with integer coefficients: for inverse images $\widetilde U,\widetilde V$ of $U,V\in D(\mathbf Z)$, the composite
$$U\otimes^{\mathbf L}V\cong S(\widetilde U\otimes^{\mathbf L}\widetilde V)\cong S(\widetilde V\otimes^{\mathbf L}\widetilde U)\cong V\otimes^{\mathbf L}U$$
is an isomorphism natural in $U,V$, since each comparison is natural. The filtered-colimit theorem denotes its value by $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N:=N\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$. Thus its application with fixed $M=C$ and variable $N=D_n$ first gives
$$H^r(D\otimes^{\mathbf L}C)\cong\varinjlim_n H^r(D_n\otimes^{\mathbf L}C).$$
Composing with the symmetry above at the source and at every stage gives
$$H^r(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}D)\cong\varinjlim_n H^r(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}D_n).$$
For each $n$, apply the theorem with fixed $M=D_n$ and variable $N=C_m$. Its reversed notation now gives directly
$$H^r(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}D_n)\cong\varinjlim_m H^r(C_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}D_n).$$
The latter isomorphisms commute with $D_n\to D_{n+1}$: the swaps are natural in both factors, and the colimit theorem is natural in its fixed complex $M$. They therefore give an isomorphism of the sequential diagrams indexed by $n$. Taking their colimit and composing yields
$$H^r(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}D)\cong\varinjlim_n\varinjlim_m H^r(C_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}D_n).$$
All groups on the right vanish when $r<a+b-1$ by step 3, so the group on the left vanishes. This proves the bounded-below conclusion from the bounded calculation.

proof.text: Assume now that all $\mathcal H^i(A)$ are torsion sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] and exactness in step 1, each $H^i(C)$, and hence each retained $H^i(C_m)$, is a torsion abelian group. For any torsion abelian group $M$ and abelian group $N$, the group $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}N$ is torsion: a tensor is a finite sum $\sum_\ell m_\ell\otimes n_\ell$, killed by the product of positive integers killing its finitely many $m_\ell$. Also $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z}_1(M,N)$ is torsion. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] identifies it with $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z}_1(N,M)$, and [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] computes the latter as the first homology of $F_\bullet\otimes M$ for a free resolution $F_\bullet$ of $N$. Every term is torsion by the preceding finite-tensor argument. Its homology is a quotient of a subgroup of a torsion group, and is torsion, because the integer killing a representative also kills its class. This proves the needed Tor assertion without bounded exponent or finite generation.

source.place: Tag 0F0F, torsion-cohomology assertion, proved here by the integral Kunneth sequence rather than rationalization; Tor definition Tag 00LY, section-tor; symmetry Tag 00M3, lemma-tor-left-right

proof.text: For every $m,n,r$, both outer groups in the exact sequence of step 3 are torsion by step 5. A direct sum of torsion groups is torsion because its elements have finite support. An extension of two torsion groups is torsion: for an element $z$ of the middle group, choose $u>0$ killing its image in the quotient and then $v>0$ killing the resulting element $uz$ in the subgroup; $vu$ kills $z$. Thus $H^r(C_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}D_n)$ is torsion. By the colimit formula of step 4, $H^r(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}D)$ is torsion as well: an element in either sequential colimit is represented at one stage, and any positive integer annihilating that representative annihilates its image. The annihilating integer may depend on the element, on the stage and on $r$.

source.place: Tag 0H80, example-kunneth-dedekind; elementary torsion subgroup, quotient, extension and filtered-colimit calculations

proof.text: The geometric point $x$ was arbitrary. For $r<a+b-1$, step 4 and the cohomology-stalk identification of step 1 give zero geometric stalks of $\mathcal H^r(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B)$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to its map to the zero sheaf, this sheaf is zero. Under the optional torsion hypothesis, step 6 gives torsion groups at all stalks of every cohomology sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] these sheaves are torsion in the locally-annihilated sense of the item. Neither argument asks for a common exponent, constructibility, any finiteness property of $T$, or invertibility in its residue fields.

split_report.summary: Statement unchanged. Proved the integral lower bound and torsion closure on geometric stalks using the bounded integral Kunneth exact sequence, then extended the calculation by two termwise truncation colimits using an existing module derived-tensor theorem. The single new node is bounded Kunneth for ordinary abelian groups, not a clause of the sheaf conclusion. All citations checked against statements. No Lean or builds. Source inequalities in Stacks 0F0F are already corrected in the item; the generic stronger tensor-connectivity node is false and is not used. Second reading replaces the off-unit symmetry descent citation by the existing symmetry theorem of this unit and writes the two colimit comparisons and their transition compatibility explicitly.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the preliminary boundedness and torsion input of lem-kun-0f0f, proof before the proper base-change reduction (Stacks 0F0F). Keeps the unit named 0F0F route. The unit has no proof steps of its own. New bounded Kunneth supplies the integral global-dimension-one calculation; truncation colimits give the bounded-below case.

tool_uses.why: The trivial-Galois field-site equivalence identifies the small etale topos of a geometric point with abelian groups; no statement of this unit supplies this generic field-site fact.
A generic module derived-tensor/cohomology continuity theorem permits two bounded truncation colimits; this unit has no corresponding ordinary-module continuity statement.
The ordinary Tor symmetry permits computing Tor1 against a torsion group in the unresolved factor; no node of this unit gives that module homology theorem.
The generic equivalence between local annihilation and torsion geometric stalks converts the hypothesis and conclusion; the unit does not prove this sheaf criterion.
